narrative_purpose: The size story in one plate: the pa'li set beside an Earth elephant and the ikran beside Quetzalcoatlus, so the reader feels at a glance how far Pandora's megafauna overshoot Earth's limits for running mass and flying span.
subject: Two paired silhouettes on a common ground line. On the left, the six-limbed pa'li standing beside an Asian elephant of similar shoulder height - the pa'li leaner and longer-legged. On the right, the great winged ikran with its fourteen-metre span set against the smaller skeletal outline of Quetzalcoatlus, Earth's largest flyer, the ikran clearly larger. A faint scale grid behind gives a sense of true size.
scene: A dark measured display space, the four forms aligned on one ground line against a faint receding grid, haze beyond.
camera: A flat side-on elevation so heights and spans compare honestly, all forms sharp.
light: Even cool glow tracing the Pandoran forms brighter, the Earth analogues dimmer and cooler to set them apart; deep indigo ground.
palette: Void-indigo background, living-teal and cyan on the Pandoran pair, dimmer grey on the Earth analogues, one scarce amber accent.
style: Painterly naturalist comparison plate, hand-painted texture, clear silhouette read.
detail_level: Crisp on the four silhouettes and their relative scale; the grid faint; background dissolving into haze.
composition: Two side-by-side pairings on a shared baseline, the Pandoran form brighter in each, generous dark margins, 3:2.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette; Pandoran forms glow from within, Earth analogues rendered cooler and dimmer. Same dark glowing-specimen mood as the chapter cover.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon or anime style
